title: Rectangular bar
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees for all axes and a translation vector also set to zero. Draw the first two-dimensional sketch on the first face, starting with the first loop. Begin by drawing the first line from the origin (0.0, 0.0) to (0.75, 0.0). Continue with the second line from (0.75, 0.0) to (0.75, 0.075), then draw the third line from (0.75, 0.075) to (0.0, 0.075), and finally, complete the loop by drawing the fourth line from (0.0, 0.075) back to the origin. Scale the entire two-dimensional sketch by a factor of 0.75. Transform the scaled sketch into three-dimensional space by rotating it with Euler angles set to zero and translating it with a vector of zero. Extrude the transformed sketch 0.0321 units along the normal direction to create a solid body. The resulting rectangular bar has a length of 0.7500000000000007 units, a width of 0.07500000000000008 units, and a height of 0.032142857142857174 units.

# Extrude the sketch

# Assign the final model to 'r'

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.075, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.075, 0.0321) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0321) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90, 0, -90) and the translation vector is (0, 0, 0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)
